transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I made an appointment, I know you probably deal with much more serious things... but I guess I came in because I've just been having a little trouble sleeping lately. 

Well, honestly, I've barely been sleeping at all since this warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just lie there at night, kind of replaying bits of it in my head. And when I finally do drift off, I wake up all sweaty and just completely wide awake. It's silly, but it feels like I'm right back near that blast. 

Is that... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
You mentioned feeling like you're right back near that blast when you wake up, is that feeling like a memory or more like you're actually reliving it?

I think... it feels more like I'm actually reliving it, honestly. And, um, I probably shouldn't make a big deal out of it, but it actually happens during the day, too. 

It's a little embarrassing, but I'll just be at my desk reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and... I'll suddenly get hit with this really sharp image of the worker on the floor, and all the soot in the air. And it just feels like my body reacts before I can even stop it. Like my heart jumps and I'm right back there in the warehouse. 

I hope that doesn't sound too dramatic... is it normal to be reacting like that?
Have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of the warehouse inspection?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it affect my work, I promise I'm still getting things done. But... I have been sort of putting off dealing with the actual file from that warehouse. 

And, um, if I get calls about other industrial accounts, I've kind of just been letting them go to voicemail for now. It's just... even when I go to open an email about those types of policies, my stomach just completely drops. I know I need to just push through it, and I will, I just... needed a little break from it, I guess. Is that... is that an okay way to handle it for right now?
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the warehouse inspection?

Well, um, it hasn't been that long, really. Just about a week. The inspection was last Thursday, and the... the explosion happened while I was there. 

So I guess it's been going on since then. I really thought I'd just bounce back after a day or two, you know? Like, it's just a week, so maybe I'm overreacting by coming in so soon... Do you think I should have just waited a bit longer to see if it would go away on its own?
Are there any people, places, or activities that you're avoiding because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

Um... no, not really. I mean, besides what I mentioned before about the work files and the phone calls, I don't think so. 

I'm still going to the grocery store and, you know, seeing my friends when they invite me out. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone or ruin their plans, so I just... I make sure I still go out and do normal things with them. I'm trying really hard to keep my regular routine going outside of the office, I promise. 

Does that... I mean, is that a good sign? That I'm not just avoiding everything?
Have you been having difficulty concentrating since the warehouse inspection?

Um... no, not really. I mean, maybe a tiny bit right after it happened, but I've been really focused on making sure my work doesn't slip. 

I've been double-checking all my math on the other accounts, just to be absolutely sure I'm not making mistakes. I might read an email twice instead of once, but I'm still getting everything done on time. I really don't want my boss to think I can't handle my job, so I'm pushing myself to stay on top of things. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble concentrating. I'm doing okay with that, right? That's what I should be doing?
Have you been feeling constantly on edge or easily startled since the warehouse inspection?

Well, um... maybe just a little bit? I mean, offices are naturally kind of noisy, right? But I guess... yeah, I have been a bit jumpy. 

Like, if the printer jams loudly, or if a heavy door slams down the hall, or even if one of my coworkers just walks up behind my desk to ask a question... I just... I jump. Like, I jump out of my skin, like something terrible is happening all over again. And then it takes me several minutes to actually settle down and get my heart rate back to normal. 

I try really hard to hide it, though, because I don't want anyone at work to think I'm being dramatic or, you know, fragile. I usually just laugh it off so they don't worry or think I'm acting weird. That's a normal reaction, right? Being a little jumpy like that after an accident?
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the warehouse inspection?

Um... no, not really. I mean, it was just an accident, right? The scaffolding just... it just gave way. 

I know I was the one who insisted we go down that specific aisle to check the inventory tags, but... I was just doing my job, you know? I was just following the protocol for the inspection. I try not to dwell on the "what ifs," because I know that's not helpful. I don't want to make it all about me when other people were there too. 

So, no, I don't think I feel guilty. I'm just trying to move past it and focus on my work. That's the right way to look at it, isn't it? Just focusing on moving forward?
Have you been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep due to being constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers?

Well, I mean... I wouldn't say it's because I'm looking for danger or anything like that. I know I'm safe in my own apartment. But, um... I guess I haven't been sleeping great. 

Actually, that's kind of the main reason I decided to come in. I've barely been sleeping at all since the inspection. I just lie there, and my brain keeps replaying little bits of what happened, no matter how hard I try to think about positive things instead. And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I... I wake up all sweaty, just completely wide awake, feeling like I'm right back there near the blast. 

It's probably just my body still working through the adrenaline, right? I'm sure it'll pass once I get back into my normal routine. I just thought maybe there was something mild I could take to help me get a few good nights of rest so I can be sharp for work. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Have you been having trouble relaxing or feeling calm since the warehouse inspection?

Well, um... I guess I'm doing okay with that? I mean, I try really hard to keep things light and just, you know, watch a funny show or read a book in the evenings. 

But I suppose... maybe I haven't been totally relaxed. Like, my shoulders are always a little tight, and I catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes while I'm working. But everyone gets a little stressed out, right? It's just normal work stress, probably. 

I really do try to unwind, though. I don't want to be one of those people who just stews in anxiety all day. I'm doing my best to stay positive and calm. That's the best way to handle it, right? Just trying to keep a good attitude?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy since the warehouse inspection?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I've actually been making a real effort to keep up with my normal routine outside of work. 

Like, I still go to my weekly yoga class, and I still like trying out new recipes on the weekends. I mean, sometimes I'm a little tired because of the sleep thing I mentioned, but I always make sure to push through and do them anyway. I figure it's really important to keep doing the things you like so you don't just sit around feeling sorry for yourself, right? 

I want to make sure I'm staying active and healthy. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still keeping up with my hobbies?
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, or like things aren't real?

Oh, no, definitely not. That sounds really scary, honestly. I mean, I'm always very present and aware of what's going on around me. 

I guess sometimes when I'm really tired from not sleeping, I might zone out for a second while I'm looking at a spreadsheet at work, but that's just normal fatigue, right? Everyone gets a little spacey when they're tired. But I've never felt like I was outside my body or like things were fake or anything like that. 

I try to stay really grounded, you know? I think it's important to stay focused on reality and not let your imagination run away with you. That's the healthy way to handle things, isn't it? Just staying present?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in since the warehouse inspection?

Um, I think we just talked about that, right? The hobbies and things? Like I said, I'm really trying to keep up with everything. 

I mean, I guess if I'm being completely honest... maybe I haven't felt super enthusiastic about my book club lately? But I still go! I just sit and listen more than I usually do. I don't want to bring the mood down or anything. 

But I'm definitely not giving up on the things I like. I know how important it is to stay engaged and not just wallow, you know? I'm doing my best to be a good sport about it all. That's the right approach, don't you think? Just keeping up appearances until things feel normal again?
Do you ever feel like you're disconnected from the world around you?

Um, no, not really. I mean... I guess I try really hard not to let that happen? Like, I always make sure to text my friends back right away and keep up with what everyone is doing at the office. 

I don't want to be someone who just shuts down and isolates themselves from everyone else. That wouldn't be very productive, would it? I think staying involved with the people around you is the best way to get through a rough patch, right? So I definitely make a big effort to stay connected to everything. I'm doing pretty well with that, I think.
Are you avoiding any specific people because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

People? Oh, no, definitely not. I'd never avoid my coworkers or anything like that, that would be so unprofessional. I really pride myself on being friendly and a good team player. 

But, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest... I have been sort of avoiding some of the work itself? Like, I've been avoiding the actual warehouse file. And... well, I've been letting calls about any of our industrial accounts just go to voicemail lately. 

It's probably silly, I know, but even just the thought of opening those specific emails makes my stomach drop. I'm still keeping up with all my other underwriting work, I promise! I'm really trying to stay on top of my normal caseload. I just... I need a little space from those specific types of accounts right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? To just ease back into the harder stuff so I don't get overwhelmed?
Has your experience from the warehouse inspection significantly impacted your ability to function in your daily life or relationships?

Um... I mean, I wouldn't say *significantly* impacted. I'm really trying my best to keep everything together. I don't want anyone to think I can't handle my job, especially since I just got this new role, you know? I want to be someone my team can rely on.

But... well, I guess I have been struggling a little bit more than I'd like to admit. I've actually missed a few deadlines on some underwriting reviews lately. And... I've started asking other people to take the calls for the industrial accounts that I'm supposed to be managing. 

I know it probably makes me look a bit unreliable right now, and I feel terrible about it. I really do. I'm usually so on top of things! I'm just hoping that if I can get a handle on this soon, my boss won't be too upset with me. It's okay to ask for a little help when you're adjusting to things, right? I'm sure I'll be back to my normal self at work really soon.
Are there any other work-related tasks or activities that you've been avoiding since the warehouse inspection, aside from the file and phone calls about industrial accounts?

Um, no, not really. Aside from the industrial accounts and that specific file, I'm really trying to just... do everything else normally. I mean, I still go to all the team meetings and help out with the residential policies. 

I really don't want to be a burden on anyone or make it seem like I'm slacking off. I'm doing my best to just power through the rest of it, you know? I think I'm doing okay with the other stuff, don't you? As long as I'm getting most of my work done, it's not too bad, right?
Are there any other situations or activities outside of work that you've been avoiding because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

Oh, no, definitely not. Outside of work, I'm... I'm really making sure everything stays completely normal. I still go to the grocery store, run my errands, see my friends... I would never want to let this spill over into my personal life and ruin things for the people around me. 

I really try to be a positive person, so I've been keeping up with all my usual weekend plans and social stuff just like always. I mean, it's really just that one specific work thing that I've been having a little trouble with, you know? Everything else is totally fine. 

That's a really good sign, isn't it? That I'm still doing all my normal activities outside the office? It means I'm keeping things pretty well balanced, right?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about avoidance of situations or activities *outside* of work. The symptom profile for Trauma_Avoidance (S070) only mentions avoiding the warehouse file and calls about industrial accounts, which are work-related. There is no information in the profile about avoiding non-work situations.

patient.answer:
Oh, no, definitely not. Outside of work, I'm... I'm really making sure everything stays completely normal. I still go to the grocery store, run my errands, see my friends... I would never want to let this spill over into my personal life and ruin things for the people around me. 

I really try to be a positive person, so I've been keeping up with all my usual weekend plans and social stuff just like always. I mean, it's really just that one specific work thing that I've been having a little trouble with, you know? Everything else is totally fine. 

That's a really good sign, isn't it? That I'm still doing all my normal activities outside the office? It means I'm keeping things pretty well balanced, right?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is experiencing symptoms consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following a traumatic event, including intrusive memories, avoidance of reminders, and increased arousal.
